title: CoordinateSectionArrows
statement: Let $P$ be finite purity data and $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{n+1}$, $n\geq0$ [def-pur-conventions]. Let $B\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be separated of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-proper-morphism], $X_r=\mathbf A^r_B$, $z_r:B\to X_r$, $q_r:X_{r+1}\to X_r$, and $s_r:X_r\to X_{r+1}$ its zero section. Put $W_r=A_{X_r}(r)[2r]$ in the recorded ordered coordinates [def-pur-affine-space-thom-map]. The projection $\pi_r$ [def-pur-coordinate-section-projection] is invertible on these finite Tate objects. Define $a_r:s_{r!}W_r\to W_{r+1}$ uniquely by $a_r\pi_r=(c_{s_r,A}\otimes1)$ followed by the canonical shifted Tate multiplication (the coefficient unitor, Tate pullback and Koszul braiding). Define $u_r:W_r\to Rs_r^!W_{r+1}$ by the specified exceptional Hom bijection [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Define the compact-support composition identification for $z_r s_r=z_{r+1}$ and its inverse exceptional conjugate $d_r^{-1}:Rz_r^!Rs_r^!W_{r+1}\to Rz_{r+1}^!W_{r+1}$ using the pasted counits [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. This conjugate is invertible. At rank zero use the compact-support identity comparison and its adjunct. The target powers are bounded below of etale origin, and all target normalizations are the uniquely specified maps above. For every scheme $B$ the coordinate identity $z_r s_r=z_{r+1}$ holds [lem-pur-coordinate-tower-normalization-induction]. For every $k$-scheme $X$ the finite ordered Tate target is bounded below of etale origin. All choices of endpoint normalization are fixed by equality with the actual unitor, factorwise Tate comparison and Koszul tensor map; the rank-one product in last-section coordinates is the recorded rank-one Cartier product.

proof.text: Use the finite-Tor Tate-power assertion target_properties of [lem-pur-coordinate-tower-normalization-induction] over Spec k. For an arbitrary k-scheme X and exponent c, pull that object back along X → Spec k → A^c_k, where the second arrow is zero. Pullback preserves bounded constructibility and finite Tor amplitude. The specified targetPullbackIso identifies the result with target X c. Thus every target is bounded below of etale origin, including c=0 and the empty scheme.

Apply the existing fixed finite-ring pro-etale compact-support projection theorem to the last closed section, with the coefficient unit and the pullback of target X_r r. Both inputs have finite-Tor constructibility by the preceding step and pullback stability. The sectionProjection definition composes this component with the functorial image of the canonical section tensor isomorphism, hence is invertible.

The one-factor, successive-target, and last-product prescribed maps have definitionally the stated endpoints. Choose those displayed maps themselves and use equality of heterogeneous-equal terms for uniqueness. For the section arrow, invert sectionProjection, compose with tensorArrow, and cancel sectionProjection to prove existence and uniqueness. All actual endpoint normalizations and orientation maps are retained.

For compositionInverse, fix a bounded-below target K. Both exceptional source and target belong to the full etale-origin class. For any object T of that class, compose the inverse exceptional Hom bijections for f and g, precompose by the inverse compact-support compositor from [thm-sf-comp-composition], and apply the exceptional Hom bijection for fg. Naturality of the compositor and source naturality of the exceptional Hom bijection identify this equivalence with postcomposition by the displayed compositionInverse. Surjectivity at its target gives a right inverse; injectivity at its source gives the other inverse identity. The coordinate exceptional comparison is this isomorphism followed by the canonical equality-transport isomorphism for the coordinate zero-section composition.
